title: The Oliver band personnel and why he never played with Oliver
summary: Jackson lists Oliver's band members, says a South Bend trip was cancelled so he never played in Oliver's band, and recounts the band splitting up and Armstrong leaving for Fletcher Henderson.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I cannot recall his first name just now, maybe before this interview was over. We can come back to it. But I know him very, Charlie Jackson. Charlie Jackson, he was killed some years later. And I joined Joe Oliver and went to play one in Gaydon with him in South Bend, Indiana, and nothing happened there. I don't remember whether it was the weather or anyhow it was called off when they got to South Bend. So I never did play in Joe Oliver's band. In the meantime the band splits up and John O'Dowd is taking the band over at the place over at the-

Yeah, Kelly Stables. And Joe Oliver, he went in with Dave Payton at the plantation. So I visited first one place or another, and Louis Armstrong, by that time Louis left the band and went to New York to join Fletcher Henderson I think. And then Louis goes and joins Fletcher Henderson. And then Ori comes up to join Joe Oliver and he had Bob Schaffner and Tick Gray on trumpets. And he had the same Charlie Jackson on bass, bass horn, and he had Albert Nichols and Bonnie Bigard on the- and Darnell Howard. Well Darnell Howard leaves the band and goes to China a little while after that. In the meantime places began to spring up. Overnight Jimmy Noon was at the nest, right in the next block, the plantation on the corner, diagonally from the sunset. Then the sunset was right across the street. And he had the band. Well this fella came from Ohio and had the band Sammy- Stewart, or something like Sammy Stewart. The bass opened up with Art Sim's band. A fella by the name of Rifferson. The same Fox had the Grand Terrace. They were proprietors. This was Sammy Stewart, or I forget anyhow. I don't think of it before this interview, I'll try it.
